# Data

## `sample_nfl_2026.csv`

**Synthetic.** Contains 17 made-up NFL players (3 QB, 5 RB, 6 WR, 3 TE) across weeks 1–9, generated by
[`scripts/generate_sample_data.py`](../scripts/generate_sample_data.py). Team codes are real, but the
players and stats are invented. Use it to try the commands and run the tests, never for actual
fantasy decisions.

It includes a few test scenarios:
- **Andre Simms** misses week 5, so he has 8 games instead of 9.
- **Kenny Walsh** is generated to improve and **Ricky Dunn** to fade over the season. The random
  noise is big enough to hide this in some weeks.

## Using your own data

Export or build a CSV with **one row per player per game**:

| Column | Required | Notes |
|---|---|---|
| `player` | yes | Must be spelled identically on every row for the same player |
| `position` | yes | e.g. `QB`, `RB`, `WR`, `TE`, `PG`, `C`. Upper/lower case doesn't matter |
| `week` | yes | Whole number |
| `team` | no | The latest team listed is shown in reports |
| stat columns | — | Any names. Only the ones your scoring preset uses affect points. Blank = 0 |

### Stat column names per preset

| Preset | Columns used |
|---|---|
| `nfl-standard`, `nfl-half-ppr`, `nfl-ppr` | `pass_yds pass_td int rush_yds rush_td rec rec_yds rec_td fumbles_lost two_pt` |
| `nba-points` | `pts reb ast stl blk tov fg3m` |

If your source uses different names, such as `receptions` instead of `rec`, rename the CSV headers
or add a preset in `fantasy_analyzer/scoring.py` that uses your names.

### Minimal example

```csv
player,position,team,week,rec,rec_yds,rec_td
Some Receiver,WR,MIN,1,6,88,1
Some Receiver,WR,MIN,2,4,51,0
```
